R16 Salvage here, 2,674 shipwrecks pulled.
During it all I noticed that the same shipwrecks have different variations. You can notice this when you are pulling it up. A shipwreck might go up by 20% each time. But if you let it go, and retry next it might only go up by 4% each time. The less % the better loot I have gotten. When doing wrecks, if it goes up by a lot, set it back down and retry until you get the hardest version of the wreck. Totally worth it, better loot.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
I'm admittedly an amateur shipwrecker, but I'll answer as best I can... There are shipwrecks which, once cleared, are counted as discoveries and award you experience for acquiring their card and discovering them, plus fame when you report the discovery to an appropriate NPC (Shipwreck discoveries are "Historical Relics"). Otherwise, no experience or fame is awarded that I'm aware of.

However, if you can get Salvage or Haul to rank 2, Oxford opens up two thesis options. The first thesis (1-star building, "100 Years of Shipwrecks") is finished from exploring a single shipwreck; the second thesis ("Sunken Dreams and Gold - Famous Sunken Ships"), however, gains pages from clearing wrecks, AND sailing long distances, and gives 1k adventure experience, as well as 500 adventure fame (assuming you're in an adventure job, of course), plus small amounts of battle and trade exp/fame. It's a great thesis to take if you travel a lot, and I use it whenever I'm not after a new Oxford skill.

It's also relatively easy to get Haul to R2, by fishing up a single shipwreck, then towing it circles with Haul skill active just outside of a port, docking once you've leveled the skill. Even if you end up not going on to do much shipwrecking, if any at all, you may want to consider unlocking the option to run that Oxford thesis just the same.

What are the dif between ghost shipwrecks and regular ones?
I think it's the NPCs and the loot, correct?

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
As I recall:

Ghost wrecks are timed; after a certain period, generally 10-15 minutes, they will fall apart, and anything not collected will be lost. JP wiki warns that if this happens while you're still inside, the wreck will not be counted as part of your overall total cleared shipwrecks.

The wreck will take constant damage as the timer (invisible, naturally) counts down to its imminent demise. Ducats and possibly equipment/items (according to JP wiki) can be lost during this time; high enough levels of Marching skill reduces the risk of this happening.

Friendly NPCs will materialize at random points throughout the wreck. Click on them before they disappear again, and you'll receive ducats and occasionally, special rare items like Headache Meds. You have a very limited window of opportunity to do this, so if there's more than one member to your fleet, I'd suggest splitting up and covering as much of the ship as humanly possible -- unlike shipwreck chests, any member of your fleet can click on the friendly NPCs to receive rewards, IIRC.

JP wiki states that while towing Ghost wrecks, disasters are more likely to occur. I've only ever gotten mine so far close to ports, so I can't comment as to that.

JP wiki also mentioned something about ghostly enemy NPCs causing status disorders at the start of combat, unless a member of your party, or an Aide, is a Priest/Missionary. It also seems to state that failure to vanquish the enemy NPCs will make it impossible to open the treasure chests.

You can translate/read more about it here: gvo.gamedb.info/wiki/?Salvaging

Two videos on YouTube also showing Ghost Shipwreck exploration also exist; you can check them out here:

youtube.com/watch?v=vxn_wnNJoGc
youtube.com/watch?v=jIJ0m0t37W8

Lastly, Ghost wrecks are found in specific locations. The wiki I keep referring to has a complete listing of all Shipwreck locations based on star difficulty and ocean zone, so you can sometimes predict if your wreck might turn out to be a Ghost version. They're pretty rare, but definitely worth the trouble of salvaging. Bring friends, good gear, and don't linger onboard for too long; you ought to do just fine.
